description: Display metadata consumed by scripts/sync_paper_status.py. Paper-local status.json files remain the source of truth for proof status, review counts, and human summaries.

FreundSchapire1997Hedge.publication: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 55(1):119–139, 1997

library_components.title: Foundations: mathematics and discrete structures
library_components.examples: Fixed-point theorems; convexity and finite-dimensional geometry; graphs, combinatorics, and counting; asymptotic analysis; Boolean circuits.

library_components.title: Foundations: probability and stochastic processes
library_components.examples: Concentration and large deviations; coupling and Wasserstein distance; conditional laws and Bayesian updating; order statistics; Markov chains, martingales, Poisson and renewal processes.

library_components.title: Foundations: optimization
library_components.examples: Convex optimization and duality; gradient, subgradient, and mirror descent; stochastic optimization; proximal maps and projections; argmax stability and envelope theorems.

library_components.title: AI and applications
library_components.examples: Alignment axioms and welfare; differential privacy and composition; algorithmic fairness; admissions policies; rating systems; recommender systems and producer/user fairness.

library_components.title: Learning and statistics
library_components.examples: Generalization and sample complexity; calibration, multiaccuracy, and omniprediction; online learning and regret; bandits; reinforcement learning; preference learning and human feedback.

library_components.title: Algorithms and complexity
library_components.examples: Online allocation and advertising; competitive analysis and regret reductions; primal-dual approximation arguments; computational complexity, reductions, and neural-network verification.

library_components.title: Game theory
library_components.examples: Best responses and Nash equilibrium; preference games; threshold strategies; multitask incentives; performative prediction and strategic responses.

library_components.title: Markets and matching
library_components.examples: Stable and many-to-one matching; deferred acceptance and proposer optimality; continuum markets and admission cutoffs; manipulation and blocking; public decisions.

library_components.title: Mechanism design and auctions
library_components.examples: Incentive compatibility, truthfulness, and payments; VCG and generalized second-price auctions; position, digital-goods, and combinatorial auctions; welfare and revenue.

library_components.title: Social choice and fair division
library_components.examples: Preference rankings and aggregation; ranked-choice voting and proportionality; indivisible goods and chores; bounded envy and envy freeness up to any item (EFX); Pareto efficiency.

library_components.title: Queueing
library_components.examples: Single-server and many-server queues; priority service and processor sharing; waiting times, workloads, and stationary distributions; heavy-traffic limits; congestion externalities and pricing.

public_summary_overrides.Naor1969QueueTolls: Few lines of code as much of machinery is in the shared library
public_summary_overrides.MendelsonWhang1990PriorityPricing: Few lines of code as much of machinery is in the shared library
public_summary_overrides.FreundSchapire1997Hedge: Few lines of code as much of machinery is in the shared library
public_summary_overrides.GHW01DigitalGoods: Formalizes the SODA paper; Theorem 8.2 uses the refined monotone-auction wording from the journal version. Formalization gap: Lemma 8.1 and Theorem 8.2 are proved for finite offer support; continuous-offer cases remain unproved.
public_summary_overrides.MSVV07AdWords: Formalization gap: Theorem 8's limit is proved when its finite-error term vanishes; deriving that condition from the paper's small-bid regime remains unproved.
public_summary_overrides.EOS07GSP: Formalization gap: Theorem 8 uniqueness is proved among common symmetric continuation plans; uniqueness among arbitrary bidder-specific plans remains unproved.
public_summary_overrides.GJ19OptimalBinaryRatingSystems: Formalization gap: Theorem 3.1 is proved for optimization of its displayed rate formula for at least three levels; identifying that formula with the actual ranking-quality exponent and proving Lemma C.4's same-objective equivalence remain unproved.
public_summary_overrides.GKGMM19IterativeLocalVoting: Theorem 3 is proved as a constrained alternative in general and as the original statement under the explicit full-space condition.
public_summary_overrides.PZMH20PerformativePrediction: Formalization gap: Theorem 3.10 gives eventual high-probability containment in dimension > 2 with uniform moments and stronger regularity; the printed sample-count and burn-in bounds remain unproved.
public_summary_overrides.LG21TestOptionalPolicies: Formalization gap: Theorem 3.1 assumes stability against profitable group entry; voluntary Lemma 4.1 assumes maximal participation. Deriving these refinements from the paper’s equilibrium definition remains unproved.
public_summary_overrides.LOS02CombinatorialAuctions: Formalization gap: twelve selected auction-theoretic results are proved; Theorem 6.1's native NP-hardness and NP = ZPP consequences remain unproved.
public_summary_overrides.LMMS04FairDivision: Formalization gap: selected components of Theorems 2.1, 2.3, and 4.2 are proved; their remaining complexity and asymptotic clauses and Theorems 3.1-3.3 remain unproved.
public_summary_overrides.PG24NoisyMatchingMarkets: Formalization gap: Proposition 1 and Propositions 7(ii)-8 have their qualitative limits proved, while the source polynomial rates remain unproved.
